issuing_body: Government of the People's Republic of China (specific issuing ministries not named in document text)
covered_actors: AI industry enterprises (large, medium, and small enterprises across the AI value chain)
Standardization research institutions and research institutes
Public institutions (enterprises and public-service units participating in international standardization)
compliance_deadlines: By 2026: formulate more than 50 new national and industry AI standards, promote and implement standards across more than 1,000 enterprises, and participate in formulating more than 20 international standards (non-binding policy targets)
implementation_notes: The 2024 edition of the National AI Industry Comprehensive Standardization System Construction Guide serves as a non-binding national standardization roadmap and technical taxonomy rather than a directly enforceable regulation. It organizes China's AI standard system into seven pillars—foundational common standards, foundational support (data, chips, compute), key technologies (including large models, agents, embodied AI, and biometrics), smart products and services, enabling new industrialization, industry applications, and safety/governance (including security testing, content labeling, ethical risk assessment, and ethics review). Implementation relies on standardization technical organizations, industry associations, talent development, and voluntary enterprise benchmarking, with no mandatory legal duties or sanctions specified. Specific issuing ministries are not printed inside the attachment text.
